full_judgment:
4. One Sinku Akramuzzaman writ petitioner-respondent filed the Writ Petition being No.1424 of 2009 impugning a notification being No.Shakha-10/1-Moti-88/82/344 dated 18-11-2007 (Annexure-H to the Writ Petition) published in the Bangladesh Gazette dated 7-2-2008 amending earlier Gazette dated 23-9-1986 whereby plot No.5/7, Bangabandhu Avenue, Dhaka has been corrected to read as plot No.7, Bangabandhu Avenue, Dhaka and thereby declared plot No.7 as abandoned property. 

 5. The respondent filed the writ petition contending, inter alia, that he is a shareholder Director and Chairman of Dienfa Limited, a Public Limited Company, incorporated in the erstwhile East Pakistan having its registered office at Ramna, Dhaka in Bangladesh. The shareholders of the Company were members of the Dhaka Nawab Family, who had landed properties around Bangabandhu Avenue and the said land was acquired by the erstwhile Government of East Bengal for creating a commercial area known as Nawbpur Shopping Area Extension, Dhaka. The then Government of East Bengal leased out for 99 years commencing from 21-1-1954 an area of 16.28 Kathas of land situated in Ward No.3, Dhaka Municipality under Lalbagh Police Station, Dhaka being plots No.48, 49.and 50 of Mouza/ Land No.TP /118/49 dated 14-11-1949 of the Consulting Architect, Government of East Bengal, C&B Department and allotted plots were subsequently numbered as holding No.7, Bangabandhu Avenue, by the Dhaka Municipality. The company obtained a loan of Taka 1,50,000 from the then Eastern Federal Union Insurance Company Ltd. by mortgaging the said land and constructed a multi-storied commercial building known as Dienfa Building and thereafter leased out most of the spaces to the said Eastern Federal Union Insurance Company Limited for its office in Dhaka. The loan was duly repaid by Dienfa Limited while the said Eastern Federal Union Insurance Company Limited continued to occupy the 1st, 2nd and 3rd floors of the said Dienfa Limited on monthly rental basis. After liberation of Bangladesh the Eastern Federal Union Insurance Company Ltd. became Jibon Bima Corporation and its Officers started to pretend that the Building of 7, Bangabandhu Avenue became a property of Jibon Bima Corporation. The writ-respondent No.3, Jibon Bima Corporation took lease of further spaces from the company as a tenant and the rest of the spaces of the ground floor and part of the 1st floor were rented out by the Company to different firms for commercial purposes on a monthly rental basis. 

 6. After liberation of Bangladesh the Company continued to be a Bangladeshi Company having submitted statement of accounts and other statutory documents to the Registrar, Joint Stock Companies, Bangladesh. Because of the death of most of the shareholders of the Nawab Family the secretarial function of the company could not be performed on regular basis. Three major shareholders of the company, namely, Khawja Sadderuddin, his wife Mrs. Chandi Sadderuddin and his sister Julekha Morshed, wife of late KG Morshed died and their shares were claimed by their heirs and accordingly an application was filed by the said heirs before the High Court Division in Matter No. 8 of 1989 for rectification of Share Register under section 38 of the Companies Act. The application was allowed by the High Court Division by the judgment and order dated 11-2-1990 allowing the rectification and directing the company to rectify the Register accordingly. The building at 7, Bangabandhu Avenue owned by Dienfa Limited was not rightly included in the 'Ka' list of notification dated 23-9-1986 published in the Gazette Extraordinary as the said building was never in possession of the government. The said notification included holding No.5/7, Bangabandhu Avenue, Dhaka which had been in possession of the government and the office of the Trading Corporation of Bangladesh (TCB) was in the said plot and at the ground floor there were other shops. The Government of Bangladesh published supplementary list of the abandoned properties of Bangladesh from time to time. But the Government with a mala fide motive included the plot No.7 through amendment as abandoned property by the impugned Gazette Notification (Annexure-H to the Writ Petition). Assailing the said Gazette the respondent filed writ petition and a Rule was issued. 

 7. The writ-respondent No.1-appellant No.1 contested the Rule by filing Affidavit-in-Opposition controverting the material facts stated in the writ petition contending, inter alia, that the writ petitioner has no locus standi to move the petition as he has not been an aggrieved person by the impugned Notification, despite the Nawab Family was the owner of the premises, they did not file any case for rectification of the holding No.7 and, as such, the writ petition was not maintainable. 

 13. Those writ petitions were filed by various persons contending inter alia that the property of plot No.7, Bangabandhu Avenue, Dhaka originally belonged to Dienfa Limited. They acquired the possession of various commercial spaces of the said building by way of some successive transfers to different persons from Dienfa Limited at different rate of rents and they 1 kad been possessing the same from the time of purchasing possession. But the writ petitioners became shocked and surprised to receive various memos dated 23-11-2008 issued by the writ respondent No.3, the Executive Engineer, PWD, Tejgaon demanding arrear rents of those space from 1-1-1972 to 30-11-2008. On query the writ petitioners came to know that the said property of plot No.7 had been enlisted as abandoned property by gazette dated 7-2-2008. Dienfa Limited is the owner of the said property and they have been paying rent to the company, but the government illegally enlisted the same as abandoned property. The writ petitioners filed Writ Petitions No.724, 725, 726, 727 and 735 of 2009 before the High Court Division challenging different memos dated 23-11-2008. 

 20. Admittedly, Dienfa Limited, a public limited company incorporated in the erstwhile East Pakistan and the shareholders of the company were members of the Dhaka Nawab family and the Government of East Bengal leased out the land of alleged plot for 99 years commencing from 21-1-1954 in favour of Dienfa Limited. 

 43. At this juncture, we advert to the matters relating to Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal Nos. 280 of 2010, 1465-1470 of 2012. It appears that the High Court Division while disposing of the Writ Petition Nos. 723, 724, 725, 726, 727 and 735 of 2009 filed by the leave petitioners relied on the judgment and order dated 13-12-2009 passed in Writ Petition No.1424 of 2009 and observed that since the property of plot No.7, Bangabandhu Avenue, Dhaka was rightly possessed and owned by Dienfa Limited, the writ respondents committed illegality in enlisting the said plot as abandoned property. It has also been observed that the writ petitioners as transferee or tenants acquired the possession of various commercial spaces by way of several successive transfers from Dienfa Limited and, as such, they were not bound to pay rent to the government. In this regard, our considered view is that since from the foregoing discussion it is proved that the government rightly enlisted disputed property as abandoned and the same is under control and possession of the Government, the writ petitioners in Writ Petition Nos. 723, 724, 725, 726, 727 and 735 of 2009 claiming right of possession from Dienfa Limited through successive transfers cannot stand in the eye of law. In fact, the writ petitioners in collusion with each other fabricated all those documents and have been claiming interest in the disputed property. Therefore, the writ petitioners-respondents are bound to pay the arrear rents of the spaces used by them in the disputed plot No.7 as claimed by the government, as the government is the owner of the property in question on plot No.7 by operation of law. But the High Court Division most illegally made all the Rules absolute ousting the jurisdiction of the government to claim arrear rents.
